title: Diagonal orientation of a vector bundle
statement:
Work in the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $n\geq1$, so $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $S$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\pi:V\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$ with zero section [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. No separatedness of $S$ over $k$ is assumed. Use the small pro-etale categories, constructible exceptional inverse image and specified Tate twists of these conventions.

Let $\vartheta_\pi:\omega_\pi=R\pi^!\Lambda_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_V(d)[2d]$ be the diagonal orientation of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]: on separated affine target charts it is the composite of diagonal base change, the normalized deformation-to-the-normal-bundle comparison and vector-bundle purity, and these chart maps are glued as in that construction. Let $t_\pi:R\pi_!\Lambda_V(d)[2d]\to\Lambda_S$ be integration along the fibres [def-amb-vector-integration], realized with the specified pro-etale twists and compact supports by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Let $P_\pi:\Lambda_V(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi^!\Lambda_S$ be its exceptional adjoint transpose, the vector-bundle purity isomorphism whose inverse is specified in [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. Then
$$\vartheta_\pi=P_\pi^{-1}.$$
Thus the diagonal orientation equals the vector-bundle orientation, with the same integration normalization.

proof.text: Choose affine opens $U_i\subset S$ trivializing the bundle, with $V_i=\pi^{-1}U_i\cong\mathbf A^d_{U_i}$ and $j_i:V_i\hookrightarrow V$, using [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. They cover $V$. The base $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. Each $U_i$ can be chosen of finite type over $k$: refine within a finite affine finite-type cover of $S$ by principal opens, whose coordinate rings are obtained by adjoining an inverse to a finitely generated $k$-algebra. The scheme $V_i$ is affine, separated and finite type over $k$, since its coordinate ring is $\mathcal O(U_i)[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$. The projection is smooth of pure dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Globally $\pi$ is affine by the relative-spectrum description in [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], hence quasi-compact and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; the finite polynomial charts make it locally of finite type and hence finite type. Smoothness and relative dimension are checked on these same charts by the affine-local characterization in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Thus all exceptional functors in the statement have their prescribed domain; every application of the DNC theorem below is made over one of the separated charts, not over a possibly nonseparated $V$.

source.place: Preparation for Steps 1-3: trivializing affine target charts and verification of the finite-type purity domain

proof.text: For a chart put $p:V_i\to U_i$, $W_i=V_i\times_{U_i}V_i$, and write $p_1,p_2,\Delta_i$ for its projections and diagonal. Let $\alpha_i:C(p_1,\Delta_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$ be [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\delta_i:C(p_1,\Delta_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_{N_i},0)$ the normalized comparison of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and $\beta_i:C(\pi_{N_i},0)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{V_i}(d)[2d]$ the zero-section restriction of inverse integration-transposed purity [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity, lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Thus $\vartheta_i=\beta_i\delta_i\alpha_i^{-1}$. This is exactly the normalization specified in the statement of [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement]. Under $Lj_i^*\omega_\pi\cong\omega_p$ from [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3), the restriction of $\vartheta_\pi$ is this $\vartheta_i$: these are the chart composites used in the diagonal construction named in the statement. More explicitly, restricting a chart to a smaller target open restricts its diagonal square; $p_2\Delta=1$ and the pullback-composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identify its $\alpha$ with the restricted one. The base-change clause of the DNC theorem identifies its $\delta$, and the base-change clause of vector-bundle purity identifies its $\beta$. The target identification is the finite-level Tate pullback of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. For two charts use affine opens inside their intersection; no intersection is assumed affine. Therefore the given glued diagonal construction has precisely these local maps, including after an isomorphism of a frame with affine space.

source.place: Steps 1-3 and the unit composite: its three factors on affine frames and their restriction identifications

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] over $Y=U_i$ with $K=\Lambda_{U_i}$. This coefficient is bounded constructible and free of rank one, so its Tor amplitude is $[0,0]$; $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and every $n\geq1$ satisfy that lemma. It gives equality of the specified smooth purity map $\gamma_{p,\Lambda}$ and the ordered affine-line comparison $\Gamma_{p,\Lambda}$. The latter is the transpose of the affine-space integration $t_p$. To check the ordered composition here, use [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]: its $d$-dimensional trace is the counit of the ordered composite of the $d$ affine-line adjunctions, each built from the restricted projective-line trace. The formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] says that adjoining a last projection $q$ changes the counit to $\varepsilon_p\circ Rp_!(\varepsilon_q)$. The transpose of that counit is, by the same adjunction bijections in the opposite order, the composite of the affine-line transposes. Starting with the identity adjunction in rank zero, induction gives exactly the ordered recursion defining $\Gamma_{p,\Lambda}$. By [def-amb-vector-integration] this is the integration used on a trivializing frame; [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies the actual integrations and their transposes on the two sites. Consequently $\Gamma_{p,\Lambda}=P_p$, not just an unspecified isomorphism with the same endpoints. This uses the existing affine model comparison, whose diagonal/DNC normalization is written in its statement; it does not apply general smooth-purity composition to prove the model case.

source.place: Steps 1-3 on the affine model, via the already existing normalized affine-space comparison; ordered counit calculation

proof.text: At the tensor unit the smooth purity map is $\vartheta_i^{-1}$. Indeed [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] writes it as $\theta_{p,\Lambda}(1\otimes\vartheta_i^{-1})$ after the twist reassociation. The defining transpose of $\theta_{p,\Lambda}$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness](2), after the tensor unit identifications, is exactly the exceptional counit $Rp_!\omega_p\to\Lambda$. Here the projection map at the tensor unit is the unit identification: in the formula of [def-exchange-projection], $\mu$ is the tensor-unit comparison, the direct-image projection map is the transpose of the pullback counit and reduces to the identity by the adjunction triangle, and the open-extension projection sends $m\otimes1$ to $m$. Hence its inverse is also the unit identification. The exceptional transpose of its counit is $1_{\omega_p}$ by the adjunction triangle. Therefore $\theta_{p,\Lambda}$ is the unit identification, and Step 3 becomes $\vartheta_i^{-1}=P_p$, or $\vartheta_i=P_p^{-1}$. This explicitly cancels the tensor-unit factors instead of treating an equality of purity maps as an equality of orientations without justification.

source.place: Step 3: pass from the affine comparison at the coefficient unit to the dualizing orientation

proof.text: The local map $P_p^{-1}$ of Step 4 is the restriction of $P_\pi^{-1}$. The actual global integration is constructed by its affine-frame integrations in [def-amb-vector-integration]. The comparison [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] says that their pro-etale transposes are precisely the isomorphisms whose inverses appear in [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. The base-change and adjunction compatibility of that corollary, applied to $U_i\hookrightarrow S$, therefore identifies $Lj_i^*P_\pi$ with $P_p$. Combined with Steps 2 and 4 this proves $Lj_i^*\vartheta_\pi=Lj_i^*(P_\pi^{-1})$ on every $V_i$, under the same source and target comparisons. This argument uses actual integration maps and their adjunctions; it does not infer trace normalization from existence of a vector-bundle purity isomorphism.

source.place: Step 3: base-change comparison of the actual integration-transposed vector-bundle orientation

proof.text: Set $T=\Lambda_V(d)[2d]$ and $h=\vartheta_\pi P_\pi\in\operatorname{Aut}(T)$. Step 5 gives $Lj_i^*h=1$ for all $i$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3), $\Lambda_V(1)$ is a finite locally constant line in degree zero; its $d$-fold tensor power $L=\Lambda_V(d)$ is again a sheaf in degree zero, since locally it is the free rank-one coefficient module (the zeroth power is the unit). Remove the common shift $[2d]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], $h[-2d]$ is induced by a unique sheaf map $h_0:L\to L$. Finite-coefficient pullback is exact termwise inverse image by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so its restrictions are the identity sheaf maps on $V_i$. The site and constant coefficient restrictions on these opens are those of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Apply uniqueness in [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] to the cover $\{V_i\to V\}$: $h_0$ and $1_L$ have the same restrictions, hence coincide. Full faithfulness and restoring the shift give $h=1_T$, so $\vartheta_\pi=P_\pi^{-1}$. When $S$ is empty this is the unique equality; when $d=0$ the affine comparison, integration and deformation are all the rank-zero identity, and the same argument applies. No connectedness or reducedness assumption on $S$ is used.

source.place: Step 3: global equality by shifted-sheaf full faithfulness and sheaf-map uniqueness; Stacks Tag 06XS (derived.tex, lemma-negative-exts (2)) and Tag 03EM (sites-modules.tex, lemma-internal-hom)

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q116-badcd0139 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the main-20261015 source with its translation/zero-section DNC proof, the unit, the citer det-sp-orientation-charts, every cited statement, and the full proofs of thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object and lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement. Statement: the added hypotheses (finite-type k-scheme S, E=Q_l, n>=1, constant rank d>=0, nonseparated S allowed) are what thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object and the site comparison need. Coefficients stay Z/l^n as in the source, and P_pi is direction-fixed. The description of vartheta_pi as the glued chart composite beta delta alpha^{-1} is exactly that theorem's DAG construction, so nothing is weakened. Step 1: pi is affine, hence separated and quasi-compact; the charts V_i = Spec O(U_i)[x] are separated finite type. Step 2: alpha, delta and beta restrict correctly. DNC hypotheses hold on separated charts. The frame isomorphism phi_i is etale, so it carries the orientation across; this is tersely written but correct. Step 3: lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement is used only through its statement (Y=U_i separated finite type, K=Lambda, any n), and its normalization is the same beta delta alpha^{-1}. I checked Gamma_{p,Lambda}=P_p from lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace (ordered composite counit) and def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction. Step 4: I recomputed theta_{p,Lambda} = unit identification from def-pur-co-smoothness(2) and def-exchange-projection, so vartheta_p^{-1}=P_p. Step 5: t_pi|U_i = a_i by def-amb-vector-integration, so P_pi restricts to P_p. Step 6: degree-zero line twist, full faithfulness and sheaf-map uniqueness on {V_i}; no separatedness of V needed. Edge cases d=0, S empty, disconnected, nonreduced, l=2, no global frame and nonseparated S all hold. No new nodes, no duplicate (grepped orientation nodes), no cycle (transitive closure checked), no SGA. I accept as tool uses lem-pur-diagonal-base-change, lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison, lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement (its proof carries the source's translation and standard-pair DNC steps), lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing and sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth. The other declared entries are in-route or Mathlib leaves and need no declaration. The split_report 'why' texts are boilerplate; review.md gives the real reasons.
